findings_to_judge.finding: The 50% Section 338 tariff on Canadian imports that took DOO from C$93.82 to C$83.67 between 21 and 26 August explicitly does not apply to goods already subject to Section 232 duties - and BRP's snowmobiles and 'the majority of ORV models' have been Section 232 derivative articles at 25% of full value since 6 April 2026, by BRP's own disclosure.
findings_to_judge.source_date: 2026-08-22 (effective date stated in document; Section 338 took effect 12:01am ET 22 Aug 2026)

findings_to_judge.finding: BRP has never once mentioned an IEEPA tariff refund - not in the Q1 FY27 call, not in the FY26 financial statements - while Polaris booked US$74m of IEEPA refunds in the exactly-overlapping quarter with ~US$40m more pending, and BRP's own FY26 tariff drag was described as falling 'mainly on PA&A', the Asia-sourced, IEEPA-dutiable and therefore refundable part of its cost base.

BRP's model-year 2027 ORV price sheet, revealed with the 17 August product launch, holds price increases near 1% and outright lowers prices on selected Can-Am Commander, Defender and Outlander models while adding factory-installed content - i.e. BRP is absorbing the 25% ad valorem tariff in margin rather than pricing it, and its CAD 200m mitigation plan is overhead and lean initiatives, not price.
findings_to_judge.source_date: 2026-08 (published after BRP's 17 Aug 2026 MY27 reveal; article headline and body describe the MY27 price sheet)
